summary: Yunxi Wang (1926–2014) was a Sinologist who studied at Fudan University from around 1947 to 1951. He subsequently held a post at Fudan University from around 1951 until 2014.
Yunyao Zhai is an Indologist and Ph.D. candidate in South Asian Studies at Harvard University (attested 2026). Zhai also holds a post in South Asian Studies at Harvard University.

Yuri Gankovsky (1921–2001) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Moscow State University (~1939–1942). He taught at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (1945–1954) and worked as a secretary at the University of Chicago (1959–1964).

Yuri Levada (1930–2006) studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1947–1952) and taught David Zilberman. He held posts at Moscow State University (~1956–1972), the Institute of Sociology (~1966–1972), VTSIOM (~1988–2003), the Levada Center (~2003–2006), and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.

Yuri Parfionovich (1921–1990) was a Tibetologist and Sinologist who studied at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (~1948–1953), where he became a naučnyj sotrudnik in 1953. He also studied under George de Roerich (~1957–1960) and Bidia Dandaron (~1965–1972).
Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University (~1936–1941) and later served as a professor there from around 1961 to 1987.

Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe. He held posts at Koyasan University, Chisan Denpōin, Shuchiin University, and served as Professor Emeritus at Nagoya University (1977–1984).

Yusho Wakahara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami. He held positions at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and Ryukoku University as an assistant professor (attested 1987–1999) and professor (attested 2011–2013).
Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at Otani University and served at Doho University from around 1966 to 2006, where he became an Emeritus Professor.

Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and archaeology, earning a doctorate from Kyushu University. He worked at Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1957–1965), Kyushu University (1971–1995, Professor Emeritus), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995–2002).

Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Toru Haneda and Hidenaka Tanaka, among others. He lectured at Kyoto University and held professorships at Tokai, Tokyo University of Science, Kyoto Tachibana, and Soka University.

Yutaka Kanazawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Ryukoku University in 2010. His supervisors included Shoryu Katsura and Masaaki Noni, and he also studied under Kōgi Kudara, Hōgei Mitsukawa, and Isao Shimizu.

Yutaka Kawasaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seio Okuda. He has held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania under Louis Renou and W. Norman Brown. He was a professor at Kyoto University (1972–1986) and Professeur étranger at Collège de France (1985).

Yutaka Takagi (b. 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1970 to 1999.

Yutaka Yoshida (b. 1954), working in history, Japanology, and linguistics, studied at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University and Kyoto University, and directed the Center of the Tokyo Raids and War Damage.

Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Hajime Nakamura at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Rissho University. He was an assistant professor at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

Yutang Lin (1895–1976) was a Sinologist and linguist who studied at St. John's University, Harvard, and the University of Leipzig under August Conrady. He held an academic post at Peking University from around 1923 to 1926.

Yuto Kawamura is an Indologist and linguist. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Kyoto University (2015–2018), and posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).

Yuzo Mizoguchi (1932–2010), a Sinologist and philosopher, studied at the University of Tokyo, Kyushu University, and Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya. He taught at Saitama, Hitotsubashi, Tokyo (1981–1993), and Daito Bunka University, and was honorary professor at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
